incidental_findings.finding: The stem teaches a false generalization: 'two identical triangles placed together along their matching edges' does not yield a rectangle in general. That holds for congruent RIGHT triangles joined along the hypotenuse; two identical equilateral triangles give a rhombus, other isosceles pairs give kites or larger triangles. The hedge 'can they form' and the option set rescue the key, but the stem asserts something untrue of triangles generally. Separately all three distractors are curved shapes, so the item is answerable by 'straight edges cannot make curves' without composition reasoning.
Omits a needed condition: two half-circles joined along their flat straight edges form a circle only if they are congruent. Seed 57 says 'identical'; seed 91 should too.

Items answer themselves. Seed 23 names two shapes in the stem and the key is 2; seed 42 names three and the key is 3 -- noun-counting, not decomposition. Seeds 11/64/103 state the parts are '2-by-2', so 'square' follows from the words rather than from spatial reasoning.

Every item describes a figure the pupil cannot see. On a competency whose entire method clause is 'using cut-outs and square grids', verbal description substitutes for the visual and physical work -- grid and cut-outs are mentioned rather than used. The Attester called this the most serious issue in the set. Also 10 items are only 6 distinct stems (11=64=103, 42=118, 57=127); circles appear once and quarter circles never outside a distractor slot.
All ten keys are mathematically correct and consistent with their listed options; no wrong key and no second option also correct.
